tag: Rolling tea hills and mist in the Western Ghats
ab: Munnar sits where three rivers meet in Kerala's high ranges, surrounded by velvet-green tea estates, waterfalls and the Eravikulam park, home of the rare Nilgiri tahr.
ppl: Most tea workers here are Tamil families whose grandparents came to the estates generations ago; they live in long rows of 'lines' houses and pluck tea in colourful saris and plastic aprons. Muthuvan tribal villages in the forest guard the hills, and every twelve years the neelakurinji flower turns the slopes blue.
go: Kochi airport 110 km; Aluva station 110 km

places.d: A bus up to grassy slopes where tame Nilgiri tahr graze beside the path.
places.t: Closed in Feb–Mar for tahr calving.

places.d: See tea rolled and fermented, and taste fresh Munnar tea.
A jeep ride to the world's highest tea estate at dawn, above a sea of clouds.
places.t: Book the 4:30 AM jeep the day before.

places.d: The highest point on the Munnar–Kodaikanal road, looking down into Tamil Nadu.
A reservoir in the tea hills with boating and wild elephants on the shore at dusk.
A tiered waterfall through tea and forest, fullest after the monsoon.
Tea, coffee and cardamom slopes spread out below, gold at sunset.

ab: Alleppey is the gateway to Kerala's backwaters: a maze of canals, rivers and lakes where rice is grown below sea level and houseboats drift past village life.
ppl: In Kuttanad, families farm rice fields below the water level, protected by mud dykes. Life is on the water: children row to school, fishmongers sell from canoes, and in August whole villages row 100-foot snake boats in the Nehru Trophy race, singing vanchipattu boat songs.

places.d: Float through Vembanad lake and canals on a kettuvallam with a Kerala lunch cooked on board.
places.t: Choose licensed boats; overnight cruises must dock by 5:30 PM.

places.d: A small canoe slips into narrow canals that houseboats can't reach, past homes and paddy fields.
A long beach with an old pier and a lighthouse open in the afternoon.
A quiet fishing-village beach of golden sand and palms.
Herons, cormorants and Siberian storks on the shores of Vembanad.
One of Kerala's oldest churches, near the sheds where snake boats are kept.

tag: Spice port of Chinese nets, Dutch palaces and a Jewish quarter
ab: Fort Kochi has traded spices with the world for 600 years: Chinese fishing nets, Portuguese churches, a Dutch palace and a 450-year-old synagogue sit in lanes now full of cafés and art.
ppl: Kochi is Kerala's most mixed city: Syrian Christians, Konkani traders, Gujarati merchants, Muslims and a tiny Jewish community share Mattancherry's spice lanes. Fishermen still work the giant cantilevered nets by hand, and evenings mean Kathakali, where performers spend two hours painting their faces.

places.d: Giant cantilevered nets lowered by teams of fishermen, beautiful at sunset.
A Portuguese-built palace with Ramayana murals on every wall.
A 1568 synagogue floored with Chinese tiles, in a street of antique and spice shops.
Arrive early to watch the make-up, then the dance-drama with drums and eye movements.
India's oldest European church, where Vasco da Gama was first buried.
Warehouses of pepper, ginger and cardamom traded the old way.
India's biggest contemporary art festival in old warehouses (biennial).
The Cochin royal family's palace with crowns, palanquins and a deer park.

tag: Red cliffs above the Arabian Sea
ab: Varkala's beach lies below dramatic red laterite cliffs lined with cafés and yoga shalas; Kovalam's crescent beaches and Kerala's temple culture are an hour south.
ppl: Papanasam beach is holy: families come to perform rites for ancestors at dawn. Fishermen haul in nets together singing, and Ayurveda is a family trade, with treatments passed from grandparents. Kalaripayattu, Kerala's martial art, is still taught in clay-floored kalaris.
go: Varkala Sivagiri station; Thiruvananthapuram airport 45 km

places.d: Walk the cliff path of cafés at sunset, then take the steps to the beach.
A 2,000-year-old Vishnu temple above the beach.
Where a backwater lake meets the sea, empty and wild.
A cable car to the world's largest bird sculpture on a rocky hilltop.
The ashram and samadhi of Sree Narayana Guru, the social reformer.
Kerala's classic beach of three crescents, with a lighthouse to climb.

tag: Misty forests, ancient carvings and spice estates
ab: Wayanad is a green plateau of coffee and pepper estates, wildlife forests and caves carved with Stone Age art, on the border of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
ppl: Wayanad has Kerala's largest tribal population: Paniya, Kurichiya and Kattunayakan communities with their own gods, songs and bamboo crafts. The Kurichiyas were famous archers who fought the British. Today, families grow coffee, pepper and cardamom side by side on small farms.

places.d: A climb to a rock cleft carved with Neolithic pictures and early writing.
India's largest earthen dam, with speedboats among small islands.
A natural freshwater lake shaped like India's map, ringed by forest.
A cluster of river islands reached by bamboo raft, with rare birds and orchids.
An ancient Vishnu temple surrounded by forest at the foot of Brahmagiri.
Jeep safaris through bamboo forest with elephants and gaur.
Walk a family farm of coffee, pepper vines and cardamom with the farmer.

tag: Elephants by the lake and the scent of cardamom
ab: Thekkady is the town beside Periyar Tiger Reserve, where elephants come down to a lake formed by a century-old dam. Spice plantations cover the hills around it.
ppl: Many of Periyar's forest guides are former poachers and sandalwood smugglers, now its best protectors, an eco-development project copied across India. Mannan and Paliyan tribal families live in the forest, and the town smells of cardamom, pepper and cinnamon from the estates.
go: Kochi airport 145 km; Madurai airport 140 km

places.d: Cruise past drowned tree stumps as elephants, gaur and sambar come to drink.
A full day of forest trekking and rafting with ex-poacher guides.
See cardamom, pepper, vanilla and nutmeg growing under forest shade.
Kerala's ancient martial art of leaps, swords and flaming rings.
A windy hill with a view over Tamil Nadu's plains and a giant Kuravan-Kurathi statue.

tag: The Queen of the Nilgiris and its blue mountain railway
ab: Ooty is the classic hill station of the Nilgiris: a lake, colonial gardens, tea estates and a UNESCO rack railway down to Coonoor and Mettupalayam.
ppl: The Toda people, the Nilgiris' first inhabitants, live in barrel-roofed huts and herd sacred buffalo; Toda women embroider red-and-black shawls. Badaga farmers grow the vegetables and tea, and every summer the Flower Show draws the whole of Tamil Nadu.
go: Mettupalayam station, then the toy train; Coimbatore airport 90 km

places.d: A UNESCO toy train through 16 tunnels and tea gardens between Ooty and Coonoor.
places.t: Book on IRCTC; first-class seats sell out early.

places.d: Terraced gardens from 1848 with a 20-million-year-old fossil tree.
The highest point of the Nilgiris (2,637 m).
Boating on the lake created in 1824 by the town's founder.
Barrel-shaped Toda huts and a sacred temple-hut with a tiny doorway.
Pine forest, a waterfall and boating on a quiet lake.
A forest-department eco-tour to a pristine lake in shola forest.
A quieter hill town with a garden, tea factories and a cliff view to Catherine Falls.

tag: The Princess of Hill Stations, of lakes, cliffs and pine
ab: Kodaikanal was founded by American missionaries as a summer retreat. Its star-shaped lake, cliff walks and shola forests sit high in the Palani hills.
ppl: Paliyan tribal families gather honey from cliffs, and Kodai's farmers grow plums and pears on terraces. The town's homemade chocolate and eucalyptus oil were started by missionary families and are now made in small family workshops.
go: Kodai Road station 80 km; Madurai airport 120 km

places.d: Boating or cycling round a star-shaped lake in the town's centre.
A cliff path where clouds roll up from the plains below.
Three granite pillars 120 m tall rising out of the mist.
Deep chasms among pine roots, made famous by the films Guna and Manjummel Boys.
A terraced farming village around an ancient Murugan temple.
Botanical gardens with roses, glasshouses and a 150-year-old eucalyptus.
A forest-reserve lake reached on a permit drive through shola forest; bison are common.

tag: French boulevards, ashrams and the Bay of Bengal
ab: Puducherry's French Quarter of mustard-yellow villas and bougainvillea faces a seafront promenade. The Aurobindo Ashram and the experimental township of Auroville are its spiritual side.
ppl: Tamil families on one side of the canal, French-speaking Pondicherrians on the other: street signs are in both languages, and some locals still hold French citizenship. Tamil women draw kolam patterns at dawn on every doorstep, and Auroville's residents from 60 countries live a different experiment entirely.

places.d: A seafront walk that closes to traffic each evening; best at sunrise.
Mustard and white villas, cafés and bougainvillea on rue Romain Rolland and rue Dumas.
A golden globe meditation hall at the heart of a township for people of all nations.
The flower-covered samadhi of Sri Aurobindo and the Mother, kept in silence.
A sandbar beach reached by boat through backwaters.
A Gothic church with stained-glass panels of the life of Christ.
Pondicherry's surf beach with a weekend flea market.

tag: Seaside temples carved from granite 1,300 years ago
ab: The Pallava port of Mamallapuram is a UNESCO site of rock-cut temples, a giant bas-relief and the Shore Temple, all within walking distance on the coast south of Chennai.
ppl: Stone carving never stopped here: hundreds of sculptors' workshops line the streets, chiselling gods from granite with the same tools as their ancestors. Fishermen of the Pattinavar community beach their boats beside the Shore Temple.

places.d: A 8th-century granite temple standing on the edge of the sea.
Five chariot-temples each carved from a single rock, with stone elephants.
One of the world's largest bas-reliefs, with life-size elephants and the descent of the Ganga.
A giant boulder balanced impossibly on a slope.
Workshops where sculptors carve temple gods by hand.
Real South Indian homes moved and rebuilt, with potters, puppeteers and weavers at work.
Thousands of crocodiles, gharials and turtles in a conservation centre.

tag: The temple city that never sleeps
ab: Madurai has been a city for 2,500 years, built around the Meenakshi Amman temple with its 14 towering gopurams covered in thousands of painted figures.
ppl: Madurai's day is set by temple time: the goddess Meenakshi's wedding is re-enacted every April at Chithirai, with millions on the streets. Jasmine from Madurai is famous across India and women wear it in their hair every day. The night ends late with jigarthanda and parottas.

places.d: A city within a city: 14 gopurams, a hall of 1,000 carved pillars and the golden lotus tank.
places.t: Reopens 16:00–21:30; phones are not allowed inside.

places.d: Shiva is carried in a palanquin to the goddess's chamber with drums and nadaswaram.
A 1636 palace of giant columns and painted domes.
Holds the blood-stained dhoti Gandhi wore when he was shot.
A huge temple tank where the deities float on rafts during the January festival.
Jigarthanda, kari dosa and bun parotta in the streets around the temple.
A Vishnu temple in wooded hills where Meenakshi's brother is worshipped.

tag: A Jyotirlinga island at land's end
ab: Rameswaram is an island linked to the mainland by the Pamban bridge, home to one of India's longest temple corridors. The ghost town of Dhanushkodi lies at the island's tip, facing Sri Lanka.
ppl: Pilgrims bathe in 22 sacred wells inside the temple, drenched by priests with buckets, before darshan. Fishing families mend nets on the beach, and Rameswaram is proud to be the hometown of Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, the 'Missile Man' president, whose family home is now a museum.

places.d: A Jyotirlinga with the world's longest temple corridor, 1,200 carved pillars, and 22 sacred wells.
A town ruined by the 1964 cyclone, at the tip where two seas meet facing Sri Lanka.
India's first sea bridge, now joined by a new vertical-lift rail bridge.
A memorial to the scientist-president with his rockets, letters and life story.
The calm sea in front of the temple where pilgrims take their first dip.

tag: The tip of India, where three seas meet
ab: Kanyakumari is the southern tip of mainland India, where the Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal meet. On full-moon days you can watch the sun set and the moon rise at once.
ppl: Every evening, crowds of families from all over India gather on the rocks to watch the sunset, then shop for shell crafts and coloured sand. Mukkuvar fishing communities, mostly Catholic, live along the coast in villages with tall, painted churches.

places.d: A ferry to the rock where Swami Vivekananda meditated in 1892.
A 133 ft statue of the Tamil poet, now linked to the memorial by a glass bridge.
Watch the sun drop into the Arabian Sea from the very tip of India.
The temple of the virgin goddess whose diamond nose ring is said to guide ships.
Asia's largest wooden palace, with carved ceilings and polished black floors.
A small granite sea fort with views of the Western Ghats meeting the ocean.
